name: NPC_Basic
description: NPC characters with basic AI, animation, and social interaction.

questions.question: Do NPCs teach real social science (game theory, negotiation, cultural dynamics)?
questions.answer: Yes. NPCs can teach game theory through trade negotiation, cultural dynamics through faction relationships, and linguistics through alien language translation puzzles.

questions.question: Can the player learn about alien cultures through NPC interaction?
questions.answer: Yes. Different NPC factions have distinct cultural values that the player learns by interacting — a trading guild values profit, a scientific enclave values knowledge, a military faction values strength.

questions.question: Do NPC interactions require real communication skills, not just dialogue trees?
questions.answer: Yes. No dialogue trees. NPCs respond to player actions, reputation, and communication style. The player must learn how to interact with each culture.

questions.question: Can the player learn negotiation game theory through trade with NPCs?
questions.answer: Yes. The negotiation system teaches supply/demand elasticity, BATNA (best alternative to negotiated agreement), and value creation through trade bundles.

questions.question: Are NPCs a feature that screenshots can show off?
questions.answer: NPCs themselves are not screenshot-friendly, but NPC-driven markets, faction hubs, and alien architecture are.

questions.question: Do NPCs differentiate us from procedurally-generated NPCs in other games?
questions.answer: Yes. Procedural NPCs with real cultural AI and educational interaction is unique.

questions.question: Can a single memorable NPC character generate social media buzz?
questions.answer: A memorable alien trader character with a distinct personality and teaching style could be the face of the game.

questions.question: Is the NPC interaction system intuitive and fun, not tedious?
questions.answer: NPC interaction must be satisfying — short, meaningful, and educational. Tedious NPCs kill RPGs.

questions.question: Do NPCs have daily routines that make the world feel alive?
questions.answer: NPCs should have daily schedules: sleeping, trading, traveling. Makes the world feel alive.

questions.question: Do NPCs react to weather, time of day, and player actions?
questions.answer: Yes. NPCs should seek shelter during storms, be more active during day, and comment on player actions.

questions.question: Do NPCs speak a constructed alien language or use translation?
questions.answer: A constructed language is too expensive. Use universal translator with cultural context notes.

questions.question: Can the player build relationships with NPCs over time?
questions.answer: Yes. Reputation system tracks relationship over time. Actions affect standing.

questions.question: Can NPCs be implemented with existing generator tools?
questions.answer: NPC AI can be implemented as UE5 Behavior Trees within existing generator framework.

questions.question: Are NPCs Blueprint or C++?
questions.answer: C++ AI foundation with Blueprint behavior trees for designer iteration.

questions.question: Do NPCs require the animation system to be fixed first?
questions.answer: Yes. The animation system needs basic locomotion and idle states. Can prototype with simple capsule NPCs first.

questions.question: Can a single NPC be prototyped in one sprint?
questions.answer: Yes. A single NPC trader in one station can be prototyped in one sprint.

questions.question: Does the AI system exist in the current codebase?
questions.answer: The AI system (Behavior Trees, Blackboard, Environment Query System) exists in UE5 natively.

questions.question: Does the NPC system depend on the generator?
questions.answer: Partially. The generator creates actor classes but not AI behavior trees. BT assets are created in-editor.

questions.question: Are NPC behaviors data-driven or hardcoded?
questions.answer: Data-driven via Blackboard keys and Behavior Tree assets. No hardcoded AI logic in C++.

questions.question: Can NPC interactions be recorded and played back for testing?
questions.answer: Yes. NPC interactions can be logged and replayed through the existing telemetry system.

questions.question: Does this depend on the character model system?
questions.answer: Yes, depends on basic character model (capsule + mesh).

questions.question: Does this depend on the animation Blueprint system?
questions.answer: Partially. Basic locomotion works without animation Blueprints. Full NPC needs animation.

questions.question: Does this prove the game has social depth beyond trading?
questions.answer: Yes, proves social depth beyond trading.

questions.question: Was this derived from the initial loop board (Loop 5)?
questions.answer: Derived from Loop 5 (Other Dots) definition.

questions.question: Does this conflict with the current AI system design?
questions.answer: No direct conflict. NPCs and scanner serve different gameplay loops.

questions.question: What AI/behavior tree knowledge is required?
questions.answer: UE5 Behavior Tree and Blackboard knowledge required. Basic BT is learnable in a week.

questions.question: Do NPCs serve the most famous educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes. NPCs with real cultural dynamics directly serve the educational RPG goal.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by building NPCs now vs later?
questions.answer: Building NPCs now means the environmental demo ships later. Tradeoff is acceptable — NPCs are depth, demo is marketing.

questions.question: What evidence shows NPCs drive RPG engagement?
questions.answer: RPGs with memorable NPCs have higher player retention (Skyrim, Mass Effect). NPCs create emotional investment.

questions.question: Does NPC interaction chain reach a human learning something real?
questions.answer: Yes. The player learns real negotiation and cultural dynamics, not just fictional lore.

questions.answer: Needs sub-features: NPC AI, NPC dialogue, NPC trade, NPC animation. Zoom deeper when scoped.

questions.question: How do basic NPC needs (food, water, shelter materials, tool repair) create a baseline subsistence economy where communities consume specific resources, driving predictable demand that players can profitably supply?
questions.answer: Basic NPCs are the demand side of the player economy. Each NPC consumes food (0.5 units/day), water (1 unit/day), and shelter maintenance (0.1 unit/day). A settlement of 20 NPCs generates daily demand for 10 food, 20 water, and 2 building materials. This creates guaranteed recurring revenue for players who set up supply routes, independent of player-built demand.

questions.question: Does the mere presence of NPCs in the canyon tell the story of a populated world — that the player is not the first (or only) person to find this place, that life persists here?
questions.answer: Every NPC is a story node: they exist because there's a reason to exist here. A prospector means resources, a hermit means refuge, a trader means a route — their presence tells you what kind of place this is.

questions.question: Can the player tell at a glance whether an NPC is friendly, neutral, or hostile based on posture, animation, and proximity behavior without needing a colored nameplate or faction icon?
questions.answer: Friendly NPCs have open posture, slow approach, and make eye contact. Neutrals ignore the player unless addressed. Hostiles crouch, circle, and animate weapons. Nameplate colors reinforce (green/white/red) but aren't the primary signal.

questions.question: Does the basic NPC's spawn state, location, and conversation flags (greeted, quest items received) need to persist?
questions.answer: Yes. NPC location, spawn state (alive/disabled), and interaction flags must persist. These are core world state. Written on manual save.

questions.question: Does the NPC character use physics-based ragdoll on death, or standard animation state transitions?
questions.answer: Standard animation state transitions. Ragdoll physics is not planned for v1. NPC death triggers a canned animation, not a physics simulation.
